stem: A flow of electric charge through a conductor is called an electric __________.
solution: Electric current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor.

stem: Materials that allow electric current to pass through them easily are called __________.
solution: Conductors, such as metals, allow current to flow through them.

stem: Materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them are called __________.
solution: Insulators, like rubber and plastic, do not allow current to flow.

stem: When electric current flows through a wire, it produces a __________ effect, deflecting a nearby compass needle.
solution: A current-carrying wire behaves like a magnet — this is the magnetic effect of current.

stem: The scientist who first observed that an electric current deflects a magnetic compass needle was __________.
solution: Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a current-carrying wire deflects a compass needle.

stem: A coil of insulated wire wound on a soft iron core that acts as a magnet when current flows is called an __________.
solution: An electromagnet is a coil around an iron core that becomes magnetic when current flows.

stem: An electromagnet's magnetism can be switched on and off by __________.
options: switching the current on and off
solution: Because its magnetism depends on the current, an electromagnet can be turned on or off using a switch.

stem: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by __________.
options: increasing the number of turns in the coil
solution: More turns of wire (and more current) increase the strength of an electromagnet.

stem: Which of the following uses an electromagnet?
solution: An electric bell works using the magnetic effect of current through an electromagnet.

stem: When electric current passes through a wire, it also produces a __________ effect, making the wire hot.
solution: Current flowing through a wire heats it — this is the heating effect of electric current.

stem: The heating effect of current is used in appliances such as the __________.
solution: Electric heaters, irons and toasters use the heating effect of current.

stem: The heating effect of current is greater when a wire has __________ resistance.
solution: A wire of higher resistance produces more heat for the same current.

stem: The coil in a heater is made of an alloy like nichrome because it has __________.
options: high resistance and a high melting point
solution: Nichrome has high resistance and a high melting point, so it heats up without melting.

stem: An electric fuse protects circuits by __________ when the current becomes too high.
solution: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when excessive current flows, preventing damage.

stem: A fuse works on the __________ of electric current.
solution: The fuse wire melts due to the heat produced by excessive current — the heating effect.

stem: The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire depends on the __________ of the current.
solution: Reversing the current direction reverses the direction of the magnetic field.

stem: An electric bell rings repeatedly because the electromagnet is __________ as the circuit makes and breaks.
solution: The circuit repeatedly makes and breaks, so the electromagnet keeps attracting and releasing the striker, ringing the bell.

stem: A device that produces electricity from chemical reactions is a __________.
solution: A cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

stem: Two or more cells joined together form a __________.
solution: A battery is a combination of two or more cells.

stem: A complete path through which electric current flows is called an electric __________.
solution: An electric circuit is the closed path along which current flows.

stem: A switch in a circuit is used to __________ the flow of current.
solution: A switch opens or closes the circuit, thereby stopping or allowing current.

stem: In the passage of current through a solution, the chemical effect can cause __________.
options: deposition of metal or gas bubbles
solution: The chemical effect of current can deposit metal on an electrode or release gases at electrodes.

stem: The process of depositing a layer of one metal over another using electric current is called __________.
solution: Electroplating uses the chemical effect of current to coat an object with a metal layer.

stem: Electroplating is done to __________.
options: protect metals from rusting and improve appearance
solution: Electroplating gives a protective and attractive metal coating, e.g. chromium on taps.

stem: A magnetic compass needle always comes to rest pointing roughly __________.
solution: A freely suspended magnet or compass aligns north–south due to Earth's magnetic field.

stem: The region around a magnet where its force can be felt is called the magnetic __________.
solution: The magnetic field is the region where a magnet's influence can be detected.

stem: An electromagnet is used in a crane to __________.
solution: Cranes use powerful electromagnets to lift and move heavy iron and steel.

stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
solution: Copper is a metal and an excellent conductor of electricity.

stem: Which of the following is a good insulator?
solution: Plastic does not conduct electricity and is used as an insulator.

stem: The wires in household circuits are covered with plastic because plastic is __________.
solution: The plastic covering insulates the wire, protecting us from electric shocks.

stem: An MCB (miniature circuit breaker) serves the same protective purpose as a __________.
solution: An MCB, like a fuse, breaks the circuit when the current is too high, but it can be reset.

stem: If too many appliances are connected to one socket, the wire may __________ due to overheating.
solution: Overloading draws excess current, overheating the wire and risking a fire — hence the need for fuses.

stem: The heating effect of current in a bulb makes the filament __________.
solution: The filament gets so hot from the current that it glows and emits light.

stem: The filament of an electric bulb is usually made of __________.
solution: Tungsten has a very high melting point, allowing the filament to glow without melting.

stem: In electroplating, the object to be plated is connected to the __________ terminal.
solution: The object to be coated is made the cathode (negative terminal) so metal ions deposit on it.

stem: An electric current can flow through a liquid if the liquid is a __________.
solution: Conducting liquids such as salt or acid solutions allow current to flow.

stem: Distilled water is a __________ conductor of electricity.
solution: Pure (distilled) water has almost no dissolved ions, so it conducts very poorly.

stem: Adding common salt to water makes it a __________ conductor.
solution: Dissolved salt provides ions that carry current, making the water a better conductor.

stem: The magnetic effect of current is the basis of the working of an electric __________.
solution: An electric motor works on the magnetic effect of current.

stem: Why should we never handle electrical appliances with wet hands?
options: Water conducts electricity and can cause a shock
solution: Wet skin conducts electricity, greatly increasing the risk of a dangerous shock.

stem: Reversing the direction of current in an electromagnet reverses its __________.
solution: Changing the current direction swaps the north and south poles of the electromagnet.

stem: A torch works by using the __________ effect of current to produce light.
solution: The bulb in a torch glows because of the heating effect of current on its filament.

stem: The unit used to express electric current is the __________.
solution: The ampere (A) is the unit of electric current.

stem: The 'live' wire in domestic wiring is dangerous because it __________.
solution: The live wire is at high voltage and can give a serious shock if touched.

stem: Earthing (grounding) of appliances is done to __________.
options: carry away leakage current safely and prevent shocks
solution: Earthing provides a safe path for leakage current to the ground, preventing shocks.

stem: An electromagnet differs from a permanent magnet because it __________.
options: is magnetic only while current flows
solution: Unlike a permanent magnet, an electromagnet is magnetic only while current passes through it.

stem: Which effect of current is used to detect whether a wire is carrying current, using a compass?
solution: A compass deflects near a current-carrying wire, using the magnetic effect to detect current.

stem: The main safety reason for using a fuse of the correct rating is that a too-high rating will __________.
options: fail to protect the circuit from overload
solution: A fuse rated too high will not melt in time during an overload, failing to protect the circuit.

stem: A material that conducts electricity better than an insulator but not as well as a conductor is a __________.
solution: Semiconductors have conductivity between that of conductors and insulators.

stem: The overall lesson of this chapter is that a single electric current can produce __________ effects.
solution: Electric current produces heating, magnetic and chemical effects, each with many uses.
